title: quantization-debug-scratchpad-nan-investigation
content:
Goal: track experiments and breadcrumbs for NaN / quality regressions that appear when serving models quantized to INT8/FP8. Mostly seeing NaNs during autoregressive generation after ~10-50 tokens for some inputs. Notes for triage and reproducibility.

Observed behavior:
- Model: redwood-open-7b / variant: rw-7b-int8-q4_0 (GPTQ-style).
- Symptoms: generations either produce <nan> tokens or collapse to repeated tokens after NaN; some runs crash with CUDA errors.
- Failure modes seen:
  * "tensor contains NaN" printed from softmax/logits pipeline in generate loop.
  * RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered (only when using bfloat16 kernel path + bitsandbytes quantization)
  * Probabilities spike to huge values (logits ~ 1e6) immediately before NaN.

Quick reproduction (env):
- Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 11.8, PyTorch 2.2, bitsandbytes 0.39, transformers 4.35 (custom runtime).
- Conda env name: qdbg-int8
- Basic repro script (inference only):
  python reproduce_nan.py --model rw-7b-int8-q4_0 --input "When the patient arrived" --max-tokens 64 --temperature 0.7

Commands I ran (local, small snippets):
- run with deterministic seed: 
  OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python reproduce_nan.py --seed 42
- try full-precision path (works): 
  python reproduce_nan.py --model rw-7b-fp16 --dtype float16 --no-quant --input-file tests/clinical_prompts.txt
- enable/disable bitsandbytes kernel fallback: 
  export BITSANDBYTES_NOWELCOME=1; python reproduce_nan.py ...

Error snippets (copied from logs):
- "RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered"
  File "generate.py", line 213, in main
    out = model.generate(inp)
- Torch check: "nan detected in softmax; logits contains NaN" (custom check inserted before softmax)
- Stack fragment:
  at aten::softmax (Softmax.cu:87)
  at inference_loop (generate.cu:442)

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quantization outliers: one or a few weight columns have extreme scale/zero-point mapping --> occasional huge dot-products -> overflow leading to NaN in softmax.
2) LayerNorm numeric instability: fused layernorm (optimized kernel) reduces precision when combined with int8 matmul -> underflow/NaN in subsequent ops.
3) KV cache mismatch: int8 path uses different past-kv layout, causing garbage reads for later steps (NaN appears only after a few tokens).
4) Bitsandbytes / custom CUDA kernel bug: certain bfloat16/FP8 code paths call into unsupported device functions on our CUDA version.
5) Softmax/logits scaling mismatch: missing dequant scale applied twice (or omitted) -> logits extremely large.

Tests to differentiate hypotheses (planned / partial results):
- Test A: run with per-channel vs per-tensor quantization map
  * command: python quant_test.py --per-channel --model-file model.pt --trace-out qc_perchannel.json
  * result: per-channel reduced NaN frequency for prompt set A (3/50 -> 0/50). Strong signal for hypothesis #1.

- Test B: force fp16/float32 for LayerNorm only (leave matmuls int8)
  * hack: in model loader, set layernorm.to(torch.float32) after loading quantized weights
  * result: NaNs disappear for many prompts but some still trigger after ~40 tokens. Suggests layernorm precision contributes but not sole cause.

- Test C: disable KV cache (force recompute past)
  * flag: --no-cache
  * result: NaN occurrence shifts (sometimes appears immediately), which weakly implicates kv layout mismatch or timing. But also increases latency.

- Test D: run on CPU with llama.cpp quantized model (q4_0) to see deterministic behaviour
  * result: no NaNs on CPU, but lower quality; suggests GPU kernel or quantization during GPU load is suspect.

- Test E: re-quantize with clamp of outlier scales (>99.9th percentile)
  * method: clamp scales to mean + 6*sigma before quantizing
  * result: NaN rate dropped dramatically in initial experiments. Points to outliers.

Commands and snippets used for re-quantize (local script):
- python tools/quantize_repair.py --input model.pt --output model_repaired.pt --clamp-pct 99.9
- small diff check: python tools/weight_diff.py model.pt model_repaired.pt --report top5\  -> top 5 changed columns are in transformer.h.0.wq and transformer.h.5.wo (suspicious).

Temporary mitigations applied to staging (dedicated GPUs):
- Use BF16 path for serving tier for the affected model; flagged as temporary in rollout config.
- Add input-based guard: if logits contain NaN then fallback to fp16 model and log full debug bundle. (rate-limited fallback)

Notes on data / prompt sensitivity:
- Clinical prompts with long numeric sequences and uncommon tokens trigger NaNs more frequently. Hypothesis: tokenization produces rare tokens with sparse embeddings causing spikes after quantized matmul.
- Short prompts tend to be stable; long context increases chance of eventual NaN.

Open next steps (priority ordered):
1) Re-run per-channel quant on full model, deploy to staging, run the full prompt suite (1000 prompts) to get reliable NaN frequency.
2) Add per-layer diagnostics: after each block compute max(abs(logits)), max(abs(weights*input)), and dump for failing runs. Implement low-overhead sampling to avoid perf impact.
3) Add automated re-quantization that clamps scales for columns with extreme max-abs before training-final quantization (script prototype exists).
4) Engage infra to run the failing prompt with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING and gdb capture if it reproduces consistently (in case of device assert).
5) Verify bitsandbytes version compatibility matrix and try 0.37 and 0.41 builds in CI to see kernel differences.

Triage breadcrumbs (what to look for in logs):
- "Scale value > 1e3" in quant loader logs (we added a warning for this)
- sudden jump in logits magnitude: store last 5 step max-logit per request
- entries in SRE alerts for device-side asserts when serving model X on CUDA 11.8

Links / refs I looked at quickly:
- https://github.com/bitsandbytes/bitsandbytes/issues/412 (NaN with q4 kernels)
- Internal PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-runtime/pull/842 (adds quant clamp heuristic)
- JIRA-788: incident for rw-7b-int8 production fallback

Scratch ideas (brainstorm):
- Hybrid quant: keep first N layers and final projection in fp16/bf16 and quantize middle layers. Might reduce outlier propagation.
- Activation clipping during inference (per-batch dynamic clipping based on rolling stats).
- Inline per-column scale recalibration at load-time using a small synthetic calibration set (cheap forward pass to compute activation ranges).
- Preemptive fallback: detect extreme token sequences (lots of numerics/unicode) and route to fp16 path.

Notes to self: keep a tight reproducible snapshot: save full container + model state + the failing prompt when NaN occurs. Capture CUDA kernel version and GPU model.

Last quick logs excerpt (2024-09-27):
[2024-09-27 14:12:05] REQUEST id=abc123 prompt="When the patient arrived"
[2024-09-27 14:12:06] INFO step=12 max_logit=1.2e6
[2024-09-27 14:12:06] ERROR step=12 logits_contains_nan=true
[2024-09-27 14:12:06] ERROR RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered

If anyone else hits this, try the per-channel quantized build + layernorm-to-fp32 hack and ping me. I'll try to consolidate scripts in tools/quant_debug and open a follow-up PR to add automated diagnostic dumps.

-- Asha
